battle.name: 陽城、滹沱之戰
battle.brief: 開運元年（945）遼太宗耶律德光南侵後晉，兵分兩路：一路取河北滹沱、井陘，打通太行；一路西入晉南，攻澤州陽城。晉軍以弩手據城牆、扼守要道抵抗，終未能阻遼軍直逼太原。此役遂成後晉覆亡之始。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 開運元年（945）交戰的兩方是後晉與契丹（遼）。後晉由石敬瑭於天福元年（936）代後唐而立，以燕雲十六州與稱臣於契丹的辦法換取遼軍助其滅唐，長期維持父子之國的君臣名分，軍政倚河東太原與中原汴州兩處重心。其指揮系統承唐末藩鎮舊制：節度使掌一州至數州軍政，州置刺史，縣置令，兵分牙兵、州縣兵與鄉兵，徵發靠括戶與和市募士，五代中期已有長兵、短兵之別。遼方以耶律德光為大汗，行南北面官制，北面官統契丹本族與諸部，南面官治漢地州縣；兵制以契丹部落騎兵為骨幹，攻堅與守城則倚漢人降軍與新附州縣之兵，糧秣自幽州、雲中諸倉儲轉輸。開局階段河北一帶的晉軍節度使多持觀望甚至倒向遼人，趙州等處守軍直接開門納降，雙方在河北、山西兩線並非同一時間接觸，先鋒與後隊相隔多日，晉廷對遼軍主力的所在與兵力判斷一開始就不準確，後方調兵因此總是慢一步。
countriesEn: The two belligerents in Kaiyun 1 (945) were the Later Jin and the Khitan state of Liao. The Later Jin had been founded by Shi Jingtang in 936, in the Tianfu era, when he replaced the Later Tang; it had paid for the Liao's military intervention with the Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun and with a subject relationship to the Khitan, keeping up the fiction of a sonly vassal. Its command system was the old late-Tang military governorship: a jiedushi held military and civil authority over one or several prefectures, a prefecture had a cishi and the counties their magistrates, and the troops were divided into ya bing (the personal guards of the governor), prefectural and county levies, and village militia, raised through household registration and through hiring in the markets; by the middle of the Five Dynasties the infantry had already been sorted into long-armed and short-armed formations. On the Liao side, Yelü Deguang ruled through a dual system of northern and southern administration: the northern offices handled the Khitan tribes proper, the southern offices governed Han counties and prefectures. The Khitan tribal cavalry formed the backbone of his army, while siege work and garrison duty were handed to surrendered Han troops and to the men of recently subjugated prefectures, with grain and provisions moved out of the depots at Youzhou and Yunzhong. In the opening phase the Jin governors in Hebei watched and waited, and at Zhao prefecture the garrison simply opened its gates and surrendered, so the two sides were not even in contact along the Hebei and Shanxi lines at the same time, the vanguard and the rear of the Liao columns were days apart, and the Jin court's estimate of where the Liao main body stood and how strong it was was wrong from the start, which is why the dispatch of reserves was always one step too late.
people: 遼太宗耶律德光是本役的統帥，會同八年（945）自幽州率大軍南下，執意再入中原；他與漢人謀臣桑維翰議定南伐之策，以晉廷不稱臣、不納歲貢為名實。晉高祖石敬瑭此時重病在身，駐節太原，只能以書檄與使臣周旋；他於開運元年八月病逝，長子石重貴繼位，是為後晉出帝，仍拒絕向遼稱臣。河東方面，太原留守楊光遠態度軟弱，與遼使往來頗為曖昧，晉廷內部對此頗有非議。前線主將杜重威自趙州、鎮州一帶率援軍北上，屢遭遼騎側擊，至開運二年正月兵困糧絕，部將王清拔刀欲刺主將，眾皆勸止，遂舉軍降遼，成為後晉覆亡的關鍵一環。河北的趙州守將趙率德在遼軍進逼時率眾歸降，被遼授以趙州刺史，隨軍南向；太原與定州一帶的晉方將領其後亦多有降者，說明晉軍在河北與河東的防線同時從內部瓦解。遼軍逼近之際，晉廷數度遣使向契丹求和皆遭拒絕，說明雙方已無斡旋餘地。
peopleEn: Liao Emperor Taizong Yelü Deguang was the commander of this campaign; in the eighth year of Huitong (945) he led a great army south out of Youzhou and was determined to enter the Central Plains once more. Together with his Chinese adviser Sang Weihan he settled on the plan of the southern expedition, taking the refusal of the Jin to call itself a vassal and to pay its tribute as the legal pretext. Jin emperor Gaozu Shi Jingtang was by then gravely ill at Taiyuan and could only parry with letters and envoys; he died of illness in the eighth month of Kaiyun, and his eldest son Shi Chonggui, the Later Jin Chudi, succeeded him and still refused to call himself a vassal of the Liao. On the Hedong side the Taiyuan garrison commander Yang Guangyuan was weak-kneed and exchanged ambiguous messages with Liao envoys, which drew sharp criticism inside the Jin court. The field commander Du Chongwei marched north with the relief army from the Zhao and Zhen prefecture area, was repeatedly hit on the flank by Liao cavalry, and by the first month of Kaiyun 2 found himself surrounded with no grain; one of his officers, Wang Qing, drew his sword and was restrained by the others from striking his own commander, and the army then surrendered to the Liao, the single act that made the Later Jin's destruction possible. At Zhao prefecture in Hebei the Jin commander Zhao Shuaide went over to the Liao with his men as the Liao columns advanced, was made governor of Zhao by the Liao, and marched south with the army; afterwards several Jin commanders in the Taiyuan and Dingzhou area also came over to the enemy, which shows that the Jin lines in Hebei and Hedong were collapsing from within at the same time. Envoys sent by the Jin court to the Khitan for terms were refused each time, which shows there was no room left for mediation.
kits: 本卡的秦弩在這場戰役裡出現於兩個位置：其一是晉軍的城頭火力，其二是遼軍新附漢軍的野戰隊形。弩機由弩臂、機、弦、矢組成，張弦後扣機自鎖，無須次次拉弦，射速與持續壓制遠勝角弓。戰國秦墓出土的銅弩機已見此制式，漢以後成為守城常備；五代軍鎮承襲此制，通常備輕弩（便於移動射擊）與重弩、床子弩（置於牆頭或木構之上，壓制城下人眾），尚有以腰力或踏張之力上弦的強弩，箭矢依射程分數等配給。晉軍的弩手多隸屬州縣兵與節度使牙兵，據城時以百步為一線分層布射：上層壓制雲梯接近段，下層封鎖壕溝與衝撞器具。攻城一方則以雲梯、飛橋、攻城車、撞竿為主，輔以拒馬槍、鹿角，並挖掘壕塹破壞守軍射界；唐末已見水砲與火藥箭，仍屬罕見。兩軍另有角弓配長槊、短兵，以及魚鱗甲、明光甲一類札甲，馬匹由北地與河東牧地供給；箭木、皮甲、糧秣大量靠騾馬與民夫車隊沿太行東麓輸送，滹沱一線失守之後，晉軍的物資線便成了致命環節。
kitsEn: The crossbow on this card appears in two roles in this campaign: as the wall-top firepower of the Jin defenders, and as the field formation of the Liao's newly surrendered Han troops. A crossbow lock is built from the bow stave, the lock, the string and the bolts; once the string is drawn and the lock is released the pull is stored, so no re-drawing is needed, and the rate of fire and the sustained pressure far exceed those of a composite bow. Bronze locks of this type have been excavated from Chu and Qin tombs, and the crossbow became standard garrison equipment after the Han; the armies of the Five Dynasties kept the same pattern, normally holding light crossbows, which were easy to carry and shoot, together with heavy and bed crossbows set on parapets or timber platforms to sweep the ground below the walls, plus strong bows cocked by leg or waist power, with bolts graded by range. The Jin crossbowmen belonged mostly to the prefectural levies and to the governors' personal guards; when defending a city they were posted in layers about a hundred paces apart, the upper tier suppressing the ground over which the scaling ladders advanced and the lower tier sealing the ditch and the battering gear. The besiegers relied on scaling ladders, flying bridges, siege towers and rams, helped by spiked chevaux-de-frise and caltrops, and by digging ditches to spoil the defenders' firing arcs; water bombs and powder arrows are already recorded in the late Tang but remained rare. Both sides also had composite bows with long spears and short blades, together with laminated armour such as scale and bright mail, and the horses came from the northern pastures and the Hedong herds. As for bolts, timber, hides and grain, they travelled by mule train and by hired cart teams along the eastern foot of the Taihang, and once the Hutuo line was lost the Jin supply line became the fatal link.
tactics: 遼軍的戰法以快速機動與多路並進為主。耶律德光自幽州出兵後，並未把主力押在單一通道上：一路沿太行東麓南下，奪滹沱、井陘一帶的渡口與關隘，直趨河東；另一路西入晉南，攻澤州陽城，威脅潞、洛，切斷晉軍南北呼應。契丹騎兵善奔襲與分割，攻城之前先以鐵騎擾亂守軍、迫其出城，再用步卒攜攻城具列陣而進。晉軍則以城池為核心死守：陽城守軍把弩手分佈城頭四隅與城門上方，先以弩矢封住接近路線，再以撞竿與火把消耗攻城器械；滹沱方向的晉軍試圖以弓弩伏擊遼軍先鋒，結果因陣地分散、糧秣不繼而崩潰。圍太原之後，遼軍放棄強攻，改以封鎖外圍、截斷援軍為主，晉軍出城反擊便退走、下次再合圍，糧盡援絕才是守軍瓦解的真正原因。降軍被遼軍整編之後仍按原編制配給器械，補進攻城與守城序列，成為遼方最省事的一支補充兵源。
tacticsEn: The Liao method was built on speed and on several columns operating at once. Once Yelü Deguang had marched out of Youzhou he did not press his main body through a single corridor: one column moved along the eastern foot of the Taihang, seized the crossings and the passes around Hutuo and Jingxing, and drove straight at Hedong; another struck west into southern Shanxi, attacked Yangcheng in Zezhou, and threatened Luzhou and Luoyang so as to cut the Jin north-south communications. The Khitan cavalry were good at sudden attacks and at splitting the enemy, harassing the defenders with massed riders before an assault so as to pull them out of the walls, then bringing up foot soldiers with the siege gear in order. The Jin fought with the city as their core: the garrison at Yangcheng distributed its crossbowmen along the four corners of the wall and above the gates, first sealing the approach routes with bolt fire and then wearing out the siege engines with beams and torches; the troops in the Hutuo sector tried to ambush the Liao vanguard with bows and crossbows, and came apart because their positions were scattered and their supplies ran out. Once Taiyuan was invested, the Liao gave up frontal assault and switched to sealing the outskirts and cutting off the relief armies, withdrawing whenever the Jin sortie forced them away and closing again the next day; it was hunger and the failure of relief that really broke the defenders. Once surrendered, the Jin troops were reorganised by the Liao, kept their old formations and allotments of equipment, and folded into the siege and garrison service, becoming the cheapest source of replacements on the Liao side.
data: 可考的時間軸是這樣的：開運元年正月晉高祖遣使至遼求和被拒，二月遼主自幽州發兵南侵，三四月間遼軍入河北，趙州一帶的晉軍不戰而降，五六月遼軍取滹沱、井陘並攻澤州陽城，隨後主力北上直趨太原；開運元年八月晉高祖病卒太原，九月石重貴即位；開運二年正月杜重威率援軍至滑州一線，糧道斷絕後舉眾降遼，遼軍入太原；同年年底澶州之盟，晉廷割燕雲十六州、稱孫於遼；開運三年（947）遼太宗入汴京，後晉亡。距離方面，幽州至太原的道路逾六百公里，陽城至滹沱直線約三百五十公里，太原至陽城約二百七十公里。兵員方面，史籍對遼軍有數十萬之說，然北方部落的動員與糧秣供應皆有限，實際出征當在數萬量級；杜重威所部援軍名冊有十餘萬之記，可見點驗數與實到之數相差甚大。弩的射程可作參照：一般弓有效射程約一百八十步，弩二百餘步，強弩與床子弩最遠可及五百至七百步（依《武經總要》一類兵書所載的量級，年代略後）。自945年秋起算，圍城一直延到946年正月，前後半年餘。
dataEn: The datable sequence runs like this: in the first month of Kaiyun 1 the Jin sent an embassy to the Liao for peace and was refused; in the second month the Liao ruler marched out of Youzhou to invade; in the third and fourth months the Liao entered Hebei, the Jin troops around Zhao prefecture surrendered without a battle, and in the fifth and sixth months the Liao took Hutuo and Jingxing and attacked Yangcheng in Zezhou, after which the main body turned north to march on Taiyuan. In the eighth month of Kaiyun 1 Jin Gaozu died of illness at Taiyuan and in the ninth month Shi Chonggui took the throne; in the first month of Kaiyun 2 Du Chongwei's relief army reached the line near Huazhou with its supply route cut, surrendered to the Liao, and the Liao entered Taiyuan; at the end of that same year the Treaty of Chanzhou was concluded, the Jin court handing over the Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun and acknowledging itself a grandson before the Liao; in 947 the Liao entered Bianjing and the Later Jin ceased to exist. As for distances, the road from Youzhou to Taiyuan runs more than six hundred kilometres, the straight line from Yangcheng to Hutuo about three hundred and fifty kilometres, and from Taiyuan to Yangcheng about two hundred and seventy. On numbers of troops, the histories speak of tens of thousands for the Liao, yet the mobilisation capacity and the supply of the northern tribes were limited, so the real expedition was probably on the order of several tens of thousands; the relief army under Du Chongwei is recorded on paper as more than a hundred thousand, which shows how far the rolls differed from the men actually present. The range of the crossbow gives a useful scale: a plain bow is effective to about 180 paces, a crossbow to more than 200, and the strongest crossbows and bed crossbows to 500 or 700 paces, following the figures set out in military manuals such as the Wujing Zongyao, which are slightly later in date. From the autumn of 945 the siege ran on until the first month of 946, a matter of some six months.
cause: 後晉的建立本身就埋下今日之患。石敬瑭以河東節度使起兵，先以燕雲十六州與稱臣於契丹的辦法換取遼軍助其滅後唐，其後年年進貢，鹽利也曾議定由兩國分取；到石敬瑭晚年，晉廷自覺根基已固，漸漸不欲再以臣禮事契丹，於是年度進貢與稱臣的交涉屢成僵局。遼太宗自居於北方霸主，認為晉廷失信，又眼見河北藩鎮多與中央不協、汴州與太原之間號令不統一，於是以收回失地與整頓朝貢為名再啟南伐。疊加天福末年晉廷內部對北方防務的爭論、石敬瑭病重造成的指揮真空，使晉方在邊境線上屢屢退讓：先是幽雲邊鎮失控，又失去河北州鎮的效忠，等到遼軍真正南下，晉軍連一場像樣的野戰都打不出來。區區一場邊境衝突之所以演成傾國之戰，起因正是這份被人為拖延了十年的君臣名分。
causeEn: The founding of the Later Jin had itself planted the seed of this trouble. Shi Jingtang rose as military governor of Hedong and first won the Liao's intervention against the Later Tang by ceding the Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun and calling himself a subject of the Khitan; thereafter he paid tribute year by year, and even the salt monopoly was arranged to be shared between the two states. By the end of Shi Jingtang's reign the Jin court had come to feel that its footing was secure and grew unwilling to keep serving the Khitan as a son, so the annual tribute and the question of the style of address settled into a permanent stalemate. Liao Taizong regarded himself as the hegemon of the north, considered that the Jin court had broken faith, and also saw that the Hebei governors were at odds with the centre and that orders did not travel consistently between Bianjing and Taiyuan; he therefore began a new southern expedition in the name of recovering lost territory and regularising the tribute. Added to this were the quarrels inside the Jin court over northern defence in the last years of Tianfu and the vacuum in command created by Shi Jingtang's illness, and the Jin side gave way again and again on the frontier: it first lost control of the frontier districts of You and Yun, then lost the loyalty of the Hebei prefectures, and by the time the Liao really came south the Jin could not fight one proper field battle. A small border clash became a war of national ruin because the vassal relationship that had held the whole arrangement together had been left unresolved for ten years.
impact: 此役的直接後果是後晉覆亡。澶州之盟割出的燕雲十六州，在往後數百年間成為中原王朝與契丹（後為遼）之間無法解決的邊界線，中原失去屏障，北方游牧政權得以居高臨下；後來北宋對遼的戰爭，幾乎全部圍繞收回這十六州打轉。間接的後果更長：劉知遠趁太原未被遼軍久占、晉室傾覆的混亂，於開運三年在晉陽起兵，建立北漢，五代以來北方最後一個政權由此成型，直到北宋初年才被掃平。此役同時把五代兵制的幾個積弊暴露在戰場上：藩鎮兵與州縣兵混雜、徵兵靠括戶、器械靠臨時造補、糧秣靠臨時徵發，平日看似兵多，一旦長途進攻便迅速崩解；契丹騎兵加上漢人攻城技的組合，則證明以少馳多的機動作戰在中原仍有極大優勢，此後宋、遼百年的攻守格局由此定型。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the campaign was the destruction of the Later Jin. The Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun conceded in the Treaty of Chanzhou became, for the next several centuries, the boundary line that no Central Plains dynasty could settle with the Khitan, later the Liao; the Central Plains lost its screen and the northern nomadic regimes gained the high ground looking down on it, and the wars of the later Northern Song against the Liao turned almost entirely on trying to recover those sixteen prefectures. The indirect consequences ran even longer: taking advantage of the confusion that followed the fall of the Jin house and of Taiyuan not being held long by the Liao, Liu Zhiyuan rose at Jinyang in 947 and founded Northern Han, the last of the northern regimes of the Five Dynasties, which was not swept away until the early Northern Song. The campaign also exposed on the field several chronic defects of Five Dynasties military institutions: the troops of the governors and of the prefectures were mixed together, levies were raised by household registration, equipment was patched up on the spot and grain was requisitioned ad hoc, so that in peacetime this looked like a large army, but once it had to march a long way it fell apart quickly. The combination of Khitan cavalry with Han siegecraft proved at the same time how great the advantage of mobile warfare remained in the Central Plains, and the centuries of Song-Liao attack and defence that followed took shape here.
result: 到開運二年正月，戰局對晉已無逆轉可能：杜重威的援軍在滑州一線投降，遼軍接管了晉軍的器械、糧秣與全部防務，太原門戶洞開，晉高祖與石重貴兩代經營的河東防線盡落。遼軍入汴京後不久，耶律德光改國號為大契丹，北中原一度淪入契丹之手；同一場戰爭裡，原後晉的降卒被整編為遼軍的南面漢軍，此後成為遼攻宋的先頭部隊，而石重貴則被貶為遼方控制下的傀儡。耶律德光在同一年北還途中病死，契丹隨即撤出中原，中原重歸中原政權之手，但代價是燕雲十六州與一個北方割據政權。五代三百年的最後一場大內亂，以後晉的覆亡收場：遼軍贏得了全部的戰術勝利，卻沒能留在中原；晉軍輸掉了河東，也輸掉了作為中原正統最後一朝的名分。
resultEn: By the first month of Kaiyun 2 the outcome could no longer be turned: Du Chongwei's relief army surrendered on the line near Huazhou, the Liao took over the arms, the grain and the whole defensive service of the Jin, the gates of Taiyuan stood open, and the Hedong line built up by two emperors, Shi Jingtang and Shi Chonggui, was gone. Not long after entering Bianjing, the Liao changed the name of the state to Great Khitan, and the northern Central Plains fell for a time into Khitan hands. Out of the same war came the surrendered Jin troops, reorganised as the southern Han army of the Liao and later used as the spearhead of Liao attacks on Song, while Shi Chonggui was demoted to a puppet under Liao control. Yelü Deguang died of illness on the road back north in that same year, and the Khitan withdrew from the Central Plains, which returned to its own rulers, but the price was the Sixteen Prefectures and one northern separatist regime. The last great civil war of the three centuries of the Five Dynasties ended with the fall of the Later Jin: the Liao won every tactical success and still could not stay in the Central Plains, while the Jin lost Hedong and, with it, the last claim of the house that stood as the orthodoxy of the Central Plains.
